skill.name: schema-research
skill.description: Researches Schema.org classes and properties for Logseq Template Graph work. It guides vocabulary lookup, hierarchy analysis, property mapping, and integration planning.

remediation.issue: Network lookups are part of the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before WebFetch or browser-opening helper scripts in restricted environments.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts accept raw lookup terms.
remediation.suggestion: URL-encode lookup terms and document that scripts only open public Schema.org pages.
Label non-executable output templates as text and separate runnable snippets from examples.

content.value_statement: Schema design for Logseq templates can drift from Schema.org standards. This skill researches classes, properties, hierarchies, and type mappings to guide accurate template expansion.
actual_capabilities: Fetches public Schema.org class and property pages for current vocabulary details.
Summarizes inheritance chains, direct properties, inherited properties, and related classes.
Maps Schema.org value types to Logseq property types and cardinality choices.
Compares requested classes or properties with existing template structure using searches.
Suggests module placement, property reuse, integration steps, and documentation updates.
Provides example research reports and checklists for repeatable template planning.
limitations: Latest Schema.org validation requires network access to public documentation.
The skill provides guidance and examples; it does not guarantee implementation correctness.
Template comparisons depend on the project files available in the active workspace.
Helper scripts only open Schema.org pages and do not perform full validation.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Class
use_cases.description: Research a Schema.org class before adding it to a Logseq Template Graph module.

use_cases.title: Validate Property Design
use_cases.description: Check property type, cardinality, and reuse before changing template properties.

use_cases.title: Review Schema Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare existing template coverage against Schema.org and prioritize missing vocabulary.

prompt_templates.title: Research One Class
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a single Schema.org class.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the Schema.org Recipe class for my Logseq Template Graph. Explain its hierarchy, key properties, Logseq type mappings, and suggested module placement.

prompt_templates.title: Validate One Property
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of one property decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the birthDate property for Logseq. Check the Schema.org type, recommend the Logseq property type, and explain the cardinality choice.

prompt_templates.title: Find Missing Properties
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison against an existing template class.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current Person template with Schema.org Person. List missing high-value properties, explain their uses, and prioritize additions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Domain Expansion
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a multi-class template change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a medical domain expansion for the template. Research core Schema.org classes, propose modules, map key properties, and outline phased implementation steps.

output_examples.input: Research the Recipe class before adding it.
output: Recipe belongs under CreativeWork and should fit the creative-work module.
Core properties include recipeIngredient, recipeInstructions, cookTime, prepTime, and recipeYield.
Recommended next steps are class creation, property additions, documentation updates, and Logseq testing.

output_examples.input: Should birthDate use a date or text property?
output: Schema.org defines birthDate as a Date value.
Use the Logseq date type with single-value cardinality.
This enables date selection, sorting, filtering, and cleaner validation.

output_examples.input: What properties are missing for Person?
output: High-priority gaps include name components, honorifics, alumniOf, and memberOf.
Location and contact properties can be added in a later phase.
Specialized financial or physical attributes should depend on user needs.

best_practices: Fetch official Schema.org documentation before recommending new vocabulary.
Reuse existing template properties before creating new properties.
Explain hierarchy, type mapping, cardinality, and module placement together.
anti_patterns: Do not add classes without checking parent classes and related modules.
Do not duplicate inherited Schema.org properties without a clear reason.
Do not map dates, URLs, or linked entities to plain text by default.

faq.question: What does this skill research?
faq.answer: It researches Schema.org classes, properties, hierarchies, and Logseq template integration choices.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Network access is needed when fetching current Schema.org documentation or opening lookup pages.

faq.question: Can it modify template files?
faq.answer: It mainly provides research and implementation guidance. File edits still require normal agent actions and review.

faq.question: Which Logseq decisions can it support?
faq.answer: It supports module placement, property reuse, type mapping, cardinality, and hierarchy validation.

faq.question: Can it compare existing template coverage?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search available template files and compare them with Schema.org vocabulary.

faq.question: Is it limited to Logseq?
faq.answer: The examples target Logseq Template Graph, but the Schema.org research can inform other structured data work.
